title: lor decodes through a bit-appended argument
statement: For every Bool a, Nat m, Bool b, Nat n: lor(bit(a, m), bit(b, n)) = bit(a || b, lor(m, n)).

formal.statement: theorem Nat.lor_bit : ((x0 : Bool) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : Bool) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.lor (AxNat.bit x0 x1) (AxNat.bit x2 x3)) (AxNat.bit ((fun (x4 : Bool) => fun (x5 : Bool) => Bool.rec.{1} (fun (x6 : Bool) => Bool) x5 Bool.true x4) x0 x2) (AxNat.lor x1 x3))))))

evidence.supports: Nat.lor_bit is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- lor_bit 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.lor_bit[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count decides the exit status. Anchored with `^Nat\.lor_bit[[:space:]]` so a future sibling cannot satisfy this row.

evidence.supports: lor(bit(true, 2), bit(false, 3)) = lor(5, 6) = 7 (0b101 | 0b110 = 0b111), against bit(true || false, lor(2, 3)) = bit(true, 3) = 7 (lor(2,3)=3, 0b10 | 0b11 = 0b11) -- a DISCRIMINATING instance shared with F:nat-land-bit's (a=true, m=2, b=false, n=3): land gives 4, lor gives 7 at the same operands, so a wrong-way `||`/`&&` swap or a swapped `bit` encoding does not land on 7 here.
evidence.notes: Applies `Nat.lor_bit` both against fully free (a, m, b, n) -- by re-declaring the statement as a fresh closed theorem over Pi/lambda-bound variables and requiring the kernel admit it -- and at the concrete, bit-differing instance (a=true, m=2, b=false, n=3), confirming both instantiations compute to the stated values.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: Reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0`, over the FULL trusted surface rather than `Declaration::Axiom` alone. The enumeration is per-environment, not per-theorem; it bounds this theorem's footprint because a proof cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type.

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*); `x0..x3` are `a, m, b, n`; the inline lambda at `x4, x5` is this prelude's `Bool.or` (no top-level `Bool.or` is declared -- see `nat_prelude/bitwise.rs`'s `or_fn`).

This is the `Nat.lor` twin of `F:nat-land-bit`, closed by transporting lane `nat-bit-decode`'s `Nat.bit` decode bridge (`nat_prelude/bit_decode.rs`) to `lor`. The fuel-swap machinery (artificially-chosen succ-shaped fuel via `Nat.lor_aux_eq_lor_of_le`, the `Nat.bit_div_two`/`Nat.bit_mod_two` decode) transports unchanged from `land_bit`. What is new: `lor`'s fuel-exhaustion guard rows PASS THROUGH the full bit-encoded operand (`bit a m` / `bit b n`) rather than land's constant `0` (matching `lor.rs`'s own absorbing-zero analysis -- OR has no absorbing zero on either side); the `n=0` guard leaf needs a case split on `a` (`or_fn(a, false)` needs `a` literal to iota-reduce, unlike `and_fn(a, false)` which collapses to a constant regardless of `a`'s shape), while the `m=0` leaf needs no split at all (`or_fn(false, b)` reduces to `b` directly and `lor(0, n)` is defeq `n` unconditionally, so both sides land on the identical raw `bit b n` expression by pure defeq). The per-bit `max`-via-`ble` combine agreement needs a split on `a` then, only in the `a=true` branch, a further split on `b` (`Nat.ble 0 y` reduces to the literal `true` regardless of `y`'s shape, so the `a=false` branch closes with no further split).

This is the `Nat.lor` twin of Mathlib v4.30's `Nat.lor_bit` (`F:ml430-nat-lor-bit-a2f98c7c`, flipped alongside this fact) -- our `Nat.lor` is itself proved equal to Mathlib's `bitwise or` specialization by `Nat.bitwise_or_eq_lor` (`nat_prelude/rec_agreement.rs`), so this closes the same proposition Mathlib states, not a lookalike about a different definition. See `docs/plan/status/258-nat-lor-ldiff-bit.md`.
